answers.explanation: Same five sections. In a query, only the header and question are filled in.
The question names what's being looked up, its class, and the record type wanted.
AA, authoritative answer. Answers from a caching resolver don't have it set.
A busy client may have many queries out at once. The ID and question tie each answer to its query.
The authority section points to who's authoritative. The additional section usually adds those nameservers' addresses.
AXFR, the full zone transfer. It runs over TCP because a whole zone won't fit in one UDP packet.
MAILA asked for mail agent records, which MX replaced.
Usually written ANY in tools. Many servers now refuse it, for reasons in the security lesson.
The host was connected to two networks, so it had an address on each. Any name can have one or many A records.
